summary: Defines the Content-Duration MIME header, which states how long a piece of timed media such as audio or video plays. It lets a receiver know the length without opening the content. It is a proposed standard that was replaced by RFC 3803.

eli5.summary: It is a small label on a recording that tells you how many seconds it lasts, like the running time printed on a video tape box.

questions: how to specify audio length in mime
how long is a voice message
subtitle: A MIME header that tells you how long audio or video plays.

tldr.problem: Receiving a voice message or video clip requires opening and scanning the content to learn how long it is. Applications need a quick way to show the duration upfront.
tldr.mechanism: The Content-Duration MIME header carries the playback length in seconds, placed directly in the message header so the duration is available without decoding the media.
tldr.outcome: Receivers can display playing time in inbox previews and on message summaries. RFC 3803 replaced it with a broader specification.

today: RFC 2424 is now obsolete. RFC 3803 replaced it with a more comprehensive definition.

sections.title: What Content-Duration Is
sections.content:
RFC 2424 defines a simple MIME header field called Content-Duration intended for audio and video content. The header carries a single number: the length of the content in seconds.

Many audio and video formats store their own duration internally, but a sender may need to expose that duration in the email header itself. The header lets a mail client show the playing time before the user opens the attachment, useful when previewing voice messages or video clips inline.
sections.eli5: It is a number in the message header that says how many seconds the audio or video will play.

sections.title: The Header Field
sections.content:
The Content-Duration header is formatted as the keyword, followed by a colon and a number. That number is the duration in seconds with no units tag (just the digit).

The value is a string of up to 10 digits. The theoretical upper bound is 2 to the 31st power minus 1 (about 68 years). The RFC notes that an exact value can only be known by playing the content, so the header carries whatever the sender determines, but clients should not rely on it for calculations requiring precision.
sections.eli5: It looks like Content-Duration: 45. That means 45 seconds. That is all.

sections.title: Voicemail and VPIM
sections.content:
The RFC singles out VPIM (Voice Profile for Internet Mail) as a key use case. VPIM messages carry voice recordings and specify an audio subtype. Including Content-Duration lets a VPIM client display the length of a voice message when listing the inbox, or when viewing on a simple MIME reader that cannot decode audio.

Placing the duration in a header makes it accessible to mail systems that do not understand the audio format inside.
sections.eli5: When you get a voice mail, the mail program can show you the length before you have to listen to it.

sections.title: Trust and Limits
sections.content:
The header value is supplied by the sender and is not cryptographically verified. Clients must not use it to determine the actual size of the data; the real length must be discovered by reading the content itself.

In rare cases, exposing the duration in a header may pose a privacy or security concern (for example, a recording of a fixed length might leak information). Implementers should consider whether the header is appropriate for their use.
sections.eli5: The number might not be exact, so do not trust it for anything important.
